blocks.text: Dohra:

After making a resolve, the Sikhs assembled (at Tara Singh's Bunga), Reposing their complete faith in God's (benevolent) Will. They started reciting the sacred Gurbani hymns, So that they might succeed in their cherished mission. (1)
lines: After making a resolve, the Sikhs assembled (at Tara Singh's Bunga),
Reposing their complete faith in God's (benevolent) Will.
They started reciting the sacred Gurbani hymns,
So that they might succeed in their cherished mission.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Now, let us look at the scenario in the Mughal's camp, Listen to their account, my dear Gursikh readers. As the custodian of Patti approached the authorities at Lahore, He narrated the account of his ignominous defeat. (2)
lines: Now, let us look at the scenario in the Mughal's camp,
Listen to their account, my dear Gursikh readers.
As the custodian of Patti approached the authorities at Lahore,
He narrated the account of his ignominous defeat.

blocks.text: Hearing this, the Nawab of Lahore felt as much infuriated, As a sleeping lion gets infuriated at someone's disturbance. The more the Patti custodian read out (the defiant) Singhs' names, The more infuriated and incensed became the Nawab. (3)
lines: Hearing this, the Nawab of Lahore felt as much infuriated,
As a sleeping lion gets infuriated at someone's disturbance.
The more the Patti custodian read out (the defiant) Singhs' names,
The more infuriated and incensed became the Nawab.

blocks.text: He felt befuddled how these wily Singhs had mushroomed again. After he had hounded and eliminated every Singh, The more the Mughals had exhausted themselves in eliminating the Singhs, The more had the Singhs multiplied in their strength. (4)
lines: He felt befuddled how these wily Singhs had mushroomed again.
After he had hounded and eliminated every Singh,
The more the Mughals had exhausted themselves in eliminating the Singhs,
The more had the Singhs multiplied in their strength.

blocks.text: At this the Qazi2 taking the Nawab aside, remarked That the latter knew nothing about the mystery of Singhs' resurrection.
He said that as many Singhs rose from the ground once again, As the number of drops of Singhs' blood fell on the ground. (5)
lines: He said that as many Singhs rose from the ground once again,
As the number of drops of Singhs' blood fell on the ground.

blocks.text: Dohra:

He advised the Nawab that the Singhs be captured alive, And their bodies be beaten and crushed with wooden clubs. Not a drop of blood be allowed to spill from their bodies, Then alone can the increase in their strength be checked. (6)
lines: He advised the Nawab that the Singhs be captured alive,
And their bodies be beaten and crushed with wooden clubs.
Not a drop of blood be allowed to spill from their bodies,
Then alone can the increase in their strength be checked.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then at such a suggestion of the Qazi, a soldier interjected, That the revered Qazi was really speaking the truth. For this (holy) cause should the Qazi be made to lead the troops, So that he could help the troops in catching the Singhs alive. (7)
lines: Then at such a suggestion of the Qazi, a soldier interjected,
That the revered Qazi was really speaking the truth.
For this (holy) cause should the Qazi be made to lead the troops,
So that he could help the troops in catching the Singhs alive.

blocks.text: He had never had an encounter with the mighty Singhs, He would never unite with his wife after an encounter with them. At this remark, the Qazi felt so much exasperated, That he could not speak a single word in his defence. (8)
lines: He had never had an encounter with the mighty Singhs,
He would never unite with his wife after an encounter with them.
At this remark, the Qazi felt so much exasperated,
That he could not speak a single word in his defence.

blocks.text: Then, the Nawab of Lahore made a pronouncement, That they must now proceed to crush the Singhs. He asked if there was any brave warrior among his troops, Who could crush the Singhs by laying a seige. (9)
lines: Then, the Nawab of Lahore made a pronouncement,
That they must now proceed to crush the Singhs.
He asked if there was any brave warrior among his troops,
Who could crush the Singhs by laying a seige.

blocks.text: Was there anyone who could take revenge from the enemies of Islam, Who would not allow the Singhs to escape and take refuge? The Hindus must be eliminated even if one broke a thousand vows, Such had been the injunctions from the Prophet. (10)
lines: Was there anyone who could take revenge from the enemies of Islam,
Who would not allow the Singhs to escape and take refuge?
The Hindus must be eliminated even if one broke a thousand vows,
Such had been the injunctions from the Prophet.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus, was Momin Khan despatched on this crusade, At the head of the command of twenty two hundred horse riders. Equipped with forty camel-loaded guns and five elephants, As well as four light artillery guns (of medium range). (11)
lines: Thus, was Momin Khan despatched on this crusade,
At the head of the command of twenty two hundred horse riders.
Equipped with forty camel-loaded guns and five elephants,
As well as four light artillery guns (of medium range).

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the herald announced the launch of this expedition, The (assigned) troops put up a camp on the outskirts of Lahore. The Singhs of Lahore who heard the herald's announcement, Understood that the crusade was launched against S. Tara Singh. (12)
lines: As the herald announced the launch of this expedition,
The (assigned) troops put up a camp on the outskirts of Lahore.
The Singhs of Lahore who heard the herald's announcement,
Understood that the crusade was launched against S.
Tara Singh.

blocks.text: These Singhs, somehow, passed the day in great stress, But proceeded to inform (Tara Singh) as the darkness descended. After arriving at Tara Singh's contingent and greeting them, He informed that the Mughal force was about to attack them. (13)
lines: These Singhs, somehow, passed the day in great stress,
But proceeded to inform (Tara Singh) as the darkness descended.
After arriving at Tara Singh's contingent and greeting them,
He informed that the Mughal force was about to attack them.

blocks.text: He informed further that he had to return to Lahore, Since he had no other refuge other than Lahore. His horse having covered a distance of fifteen miles, Must he return to Lahore (before day break)for his survival. (14)
lines: He informed further that he had to return to Lahore,
Since he had no other refuge other than Lahore.
His horse having covered a distance of fifteen miles,
Must he return to Lahore (before day break)for his survival.

blocks.text: Dohra:

He advised Tara Singh and his companions, That they had no other option except to hibernate themselves. They had only one night for these maneavours, As the Mughal troops would be upon them with the day break. (15)
lines: He advised Tara Singh and his companions,
That they had no other option except to hibernate themselves.
They had only one night for these maneavours,
As the Mughal troops would be upon them with the day break.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The messenger returned after giving this information, But (dear readers), listen how did Tara Singh react. Tara Singh feeling extremely charged with emotion, remarked, That he himself was too keen to sacrifice to stigmatise the Mughals. (16)
lines: The messenger returned after giving this information,
But (dear readers), listen how did Tara Singh react.
Tara Singh feeling extremely charged with emotion, remarked,
That he himself was too keen to sacrifice to stigmatise the Mughals.

blocks.text: He would fight to the finish at his own camp, Nor would he desert his place to find escape elsewhere. Instead of seeking a refuge in the dense wilds, He would prefer to confront death in a straight fight. (17)
lines: He would fight to the finish at his own camp,
Nor would he desert his place to find escape elsewhere.
Instead of seeking a refuge in the dense wilds,
He would prefer to confront death in a straight fight.

blocks.text: Where could one seek shelter by taking a flight, Where could one remain untraced by death. Death kept a trail of us (like our shadow), As had been revealed by revered Satguru's words. (18)
lines: Where could one seek shelter by taking a flight,
Where could one remain untraced by death.
Death kept a trail of us (like our shadow),
As had been revealed by revered Satguru's words.

blocks.text: Savaiya : If one could escape death by taking a flight, Then which direction should one choose for fleeing? When death is looming large wherever one goes, How can one run back from the looming death? No one has ever devised any such technique, Which one could exploit to escape death's fatal blow, When nothing avails Oh! foolish human being, Why don't you smilingly submit before death? (Bachittar Natak-96)
